````` ::: ::: ### Nest description The nest is an open cup of rootlets and plant fibers lined with plant down, often woven so tightly that it can hold water. The female lashes the foundation to supporting branches using spider silk, and makes a downy lining often using the fluffy “pappus” material taken from the same types of seedheads that goldfinches so commonly feed on. It takes the female about 6 days to build the nest. The finished nest is about 3 inches across on the outside and 2-4.5 inches high. ![](images/agol_nest.jpg){.intro_image} ### Egg description ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
